source_title: Scale-Up of Alfalfa (Medicago sativa) Protein Recovery Using Screw Presses
authors: Mikkel Hansen; Christina Albers Andersen; Peter Ruhdal Jensen; Timothy John Hobley
source_location: Methods §2.1; Table 1; Table 2; Table A1; Abstract; Results §3.1 and Conclusions
geography: Fyn, Denmark; alfalfa harvested in spring 2019
evidence_class: Primary experimental literature; measurements and source-reported cumulative recovery
measurement_basis: Single-screw pilot press, 50.8 kg initial fresh whole-alfalfa batch; feed reported to contain 2189 g protein. Working pressure 6 bar, 10 rpm, 0.5 mm filter. Pulp rehydrated with tap water at twice pulp mass before each subsequent pass. Source tables report mass in g and APC composition on dry matter basis.
uncertainty: Table 2 values are mean ± standard deviation, n=3, for protein content and protein digestibility. Table A1 fraction masses are reported without uncertainty. Cumulative total-protein recovery is reported at the first, second, and tenth pass only; other pass-specific cumulative values are not reported.
conversion_and_scaling: No values converted. Source's % DM basis and g mass units are retained. Pressing, juice precipitation, centrifugation, and freeze-drying are laboratory/pilot-specific; do not scale as a GreenHub design equation.
applicability: Reusable as a traceable alfalfa screw-press and product-quality comparator for alternative green-biomass projects after matching equipment and feed basis.
limitations: Feedstock is alfalfa, not roadside grass or GreenHub feed.
The reported ten-pass sequence includes repeated water addition and does not imply industrial feasibility.
Centrifugation followed acidification of juice to pH 3.5; the recovered concentrate was freeze-dried.
The authors report over 14% of wet input mass unaccounted in Table 1 and note repeated pressing uses substantial water, time, and energy.
No source data are calculation-connected in GreenHub; do not use as a default or direct isoelectric precipitation yield.
